s1.syndrome_frame: Acute liver injury with obstructive uropathy
salient_findings: Generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, γ-glutamyl transferase)
key_facts: 65-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia
Prostate-specific antigen level was 0.796 ng/mL
Uroflowmetry revealed reduced urine flow, prolonged micturition time, and obstructive findings
Started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily
Developed symptoms on day 9 of therapy
Denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines
No history of liver disease
Jaundiced but no stigmata of chronic liver disease on examination
Leukocyte count 5.8 K/μL
Elevated liver enzymes (AST 175 U/L, ALT 402 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 235 U/L, γ-glutamyl transferase 327 U/L)
Hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 7.6 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL)
Normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts on abdominal ultrasonography
Negative serologic tests for viral hepatitis and autoimmune markers

shortlist.label: Drug-induced liver injury
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed symptoms after starting Alfuzosin, and laboratory results show elevated liver enzymes and hyperbilirubinemia

shortlist.label: Alfuzosin-induced cholestasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was taking Alfuzosin when symptoms developed, and cholestasis is a known side effect of this medication

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholestasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated liver enzymes and hyperbilirubinemia, consistent with intrahepatic cholestasis

shortlist.label: Primary biliary cholangitis
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, primary biliary cholangitis can cause cholestasis and elevated liver enzymes, and should be considered in the differential diagnosis

shortlist.label: Autoimmune hepatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Although autoimmune markers were negative, autoimmune hepatitis can still be a consideration, especially given the patient's elevated liver enzymes and hyperbilirubinemia
